claims.explanation: Nitrofurazone is a nitroaromatic prodrug that requires reductive bioactivation by nitroreductases (NTR/NfsA/NfsB family flavin enzymes) to generate cytotoxic hydroxylamine/nitroso intermediates; mammalian cells with high expression of homologous nitroreductases (e.g., NQO1, NQO2, POR) should activate the drug more efficiently and be selectively killed, while low expression or high detoxifying capacity protects. The hypoxic selectivity seen in mammalian cells (PMID 1253180) and the requirement for two-electron nitroreduction (PMIDs 15684426, 1999405) suggest that oxygen-insensitive reductases and the cellular redox environment determine sensitivity. The virtual-cell response (CDKN1A induction, oxidative-stress genes) is consistent with DNA damage and oxidative stress rather than a specific

features.basis: NQO1 is a mammalian two-electron nitroreductase homologous to bacterial NfsA/NfsB that bioactivates nitroaromatics like CB1954 and nitrofurazone (PMID 1472094)
NQO2 is a flavin-dependent quinone/nitroreductase capable of reducing nitroaromatic prodrugs to cytotoxic species
NADPH-cytochrome P450 oxidoreductase can reductively activate nitroaromatic compounds, generating reactive intermediates
High cysteine desulfurase/flavin availability may alter redox balance and reduce nitroreductive drug activation
Loss of p53 would impair DNA-damage-induced apoptosis, reducing sensitivity to nitrofurazone-induced DNA damage
Virtual cell shows CDKN1A induction at 24 h; p21 upregulation may arrest cells and limit drug-induced lethality
Constitutive NRF2 activation increases antioxidant capacity, countering nitrofurazone-induced oxidative stress
KEAP1 loss activates NRF2 and antioxidant programs that detoxify reactive oxygen species from nitroreduction
G6PD supplies NADPH for nitroreductase-mediated bioactivation and for glutathione recycling
CYP2S1 is a hypoxia-inducible oxidoreductase that can reductively metabolize nitroaromatic drugs
Hypoxia increases nitrofurazone cytotoxicity (PMID 1253180); HIF1A-high tumors may mimic hypoxic activation
Aldo-keto reductase 1C3 can reduce nitroaromatic compounds and contribute to prodrug activation
